title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Deep Field. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Deep Field
options.lineage: JWST / Hubble deep-field astrophotography and its catalog annotations
options.thesis: The portfolio is one Webb deep field you point the telescope into; every galaxy in it is a piece of Leon's work.
materials: thin reticle circles and catalog labels
options.viewport: A full-bleed deep field. Leon's name sits in the corner as the field's designation, galaxies are circled and labelled as projects and career stops, and a filter wheel at the bottom re-lenses the whole field.
options.risk: Dark space is what visitors expect, so it only stands out if the real imagery and strict catalog discipline carry it, not glow effects.

raised.raise: Colour by role: each filter colour belongs to one kind of content (work, career, skills, contact) and is never decoration.
One control remaps everything: turning the filter wheel re-lenses the entire field at once.
A persistent pointing readout (RA/Dec, field of view, filter) always tells you where you are.
Every target has an explicit state vocabulary: unresolved, acquired, resolved.
Labels stay set, readable text through every zoom and transition.

options.label: Golden Record
options.lineage: the 1977 Voyager Golden Record cover and its engraved instruction diagrams
options.thesis: Leon's portfolio as a message for strangers: an engraved gold record whose diagrams teach you how to read him.
options.viewport: The record's face fills the screen. The pulsar-map rays are the navigation, each one leading to a chapter: work, career, skills and contact.
options.risk: My top-ranked idea; a disc is a less natural explorable system than a field, and gold engraving can feel static if the motion is weak.

options.label: Star Course
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps, translated into a deep-space chart
options.thesis: Space drawn as an orienteering chart: gravity wells as contours, with a numbered purple course leading control to control through Leon's work.
options.viewport: A chart of space with contour fields; the purple course runs from the start triangle through numbered controls (projects, career) to the finish (contact), with the legend top right.
options.case: It fuses cleanly and holds on product clarity (a guided route through the work), but loses on identification: peers don't read orienteering as space.
options.risk: Can read as a hiking map with a space skin if the contour fields aren't convincingly cosmic.

options.label: Bauhaus Workshop
options.thesis: Projects as primary forms arranged on a white worktable.
options.viewport: Primary shapes composed on a white ground.
options.risk: It drops the space world that PRODUCT.md binds.
options.case: It loses on both axes: no space identity, and the projects become abstractions.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Words condense into weather and landscape.
options.viewport: Letters gather into words across white ground.
options.risk: A white paper world, unrelated to space.
options.case: It loses on both axes: off-world, and the work disappears behind the type.
options.kept: Text stays readable through every transformation.

options.label: Miura Orbit Sheet
options.thesis: A packet that unfolds into the whole portfolio.
options.viewport: A gold packet unfolding into a tessellated sheet.
options.risk: A paper engineering piece that is only adjacent to space.
options.case: It loses on both axes: weak self-representation, and no explorable system.
options.kept: An explicit state vocabulary for every object.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One axis slider morphs the whole page.
options.viewport: A giant glyph with an axis slider.
options.risk: Not space; it's about fonts, not Leon.
options.kept: One control continuously remaps the entire surface.

options.label: Step Row
options.thesis: The career as a sixteen-step pattern.
options.viewport: A sixteen-step row under a chase light.
options.kept: A persistent indicator of where 'now' is.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The familiar space dev portfolio: a 3D planet hero, a nebula backdrop and glass project cards, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and tagline beside a rotating 3D planet, with a row of project cards below.
canonCard.risk: It looks like every other space portfolio, by design.
